title: A hyper-parameter tuning approach for cost-sensitive support vector machine classifiers
authors: Guido, R.; Groccia, M. C.; Conforti, D.
tldr: Proposes a multi-objective genetic algorithm approach for tuning cost-sensitive SVM hyper-parameters, with improved GA+DT version reducing computation time on imbalanced data.
problem_and_motivation: Class imbalance degrades classifier performance and hyper-parameter tuning is computationally expensive. Existing methods do not jointly optimize multiple imbalanced data performance measures.
approach: Develops bi-objective optimization maximizing balanced accuracy and minimizing false positive rate for SVM.
Basic version uses genetic algorithms to search SVM cost, gamma, and class-weight parameters.
Improved version combines genetic algorithms with decision trees to reduce computational time.
Tests approach on benchmark imbalanced datasets from UCI repository.
Implements both serial and parallel versions.
findings: num: Improved GA+DT version strongly reduces computational time compared to basic GA version.
Multi-objective optimization finds SVM configurations balancing sensitivity and specificity.
Suitable evaluation measures (balanced accuracy, G-mean) are critical for imbalanced data.
Parallel implementation scales effectively across multiple processors.

definitions.definition: SVM with different misclassification costs per class.
Geometric mean of sensitivity and specificity.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Proposes multi-objective hyper-parameter tuning for SVM on imbalanced datasets. Demonstrates GA+DT combination reduces optimization time. Highlights appropriate evaluation metrics for imbalanced classification.
directly_justifies: Multi-objective GA improves SVM on imbalanced data.
GA+DT combination reduces hyper-parameter search time.
